h1: The Validity Numbers and Adverse-Impact Data Behind Psychometric Hiring Tests

persona.name: Executive & Compliance Buyer
persona.lens: A CHRO or legally-minded enterprise/OFCCP HR leader who is answerable for the selection process in court or the boardroom, and needs per-assessment-type validity and adverse-impact evidence to defend which tests the company uses under EEOC Uniform Guidelines.
persona.why: The topic is predictive-validity research and EEOC adverse-impact records per assessment type plus an enforcement shift — this is defensibility/compliance risk content, which the doc routes to the Executive & Compliance Buyer, not the recruiter who merely runs screening.

gaps_to_own: No readable competitor ties disparate impact to actual assessment types (cognitive, personality, situational judgment, etc.) or shows predictive-validity research per type — this is the core of the distinct angle and appears fully open.

winners_drift: The one readable page (jacksonlewis.com) is a law-firm legal update on a 2025 Executive Order pushing to eliminate disparate impact liability — it covers litigation/compliance risk for employers generally, not hiring assessments specifically, and never engages predictive validity or per-assessment-type evidence.

Duke Power Co. 1971), Housing (Fair Housing Act), Recent Shifts (federal pullback on disparate-impact enforcement).
